6 Orthopedic Denial Patterns. Each Costing Your Practice Thousands Per Month

Orthopedic denials compound differently than other specialties. One global period miscalculation denies every follow-up visit for 90 days. One wrong modifier repeats on every similar surgical case. PMEX eliminates each pattern at the root.

PATTERN 01

E/M Billed During Active 90-Day Surgical Window

Total knee replacement performed June 1. Follow-up visit billed September 3, Day 94 of the 90-day global period. Medicare auto-denies the E/M as duplicate of the surgical payment. Error repeats on every follow-up for every patient in the global window.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX pulls procedure dates from your operative notes and tracks every active global period across your entire patient panel. Modifier 24 applied for unrelated E/M during global. Modifier 79 applied for unrelated procedures. No global period violation ever submitted.

PATTERN 02

Return-to-OR Modifier Applied to Wrong Clinical Scenario

Patient returns to OR during global period for wound debridement (related to the original surgery). Billed with Modifier 79 (unrelated procedure). Payer denies, Modifier 58 (staged/planned), 78 (related return), or 79 (unrelated return) was required. Audit flag created for systematic modifier misuse across all surgical returns.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX reviews operative notes for clinical context on every return-to-OR claim. Modifier 58 (staged/planned), 78 (related return), or 79 (unrelated return) applied based on the documented relationship to the original procedure. Correct modifier on every surgical return claim.

PATTERN 03

Wrong State Form or Fee Schedule Applied to WC Claims

Texas WC claim submitted on CMS-1500 form instead of the Texas-specific DWC-73/OWCP form. California WC claim reimbursed at the wrong fee schedule tier. Both are systematic errors that underpay or deny every WC claim in that state until someone catches the pattern.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX manages WC billing as a dedicated, state-specific workflow, correct forms, state-specific fee schedules, employer/insurer routing, and authorization requirements for all 50 state workers' comp programs. Not one WC claim leaves with the wrong form or fee schedule.

PATTERN 04

Separately Billed Procedures Inclusive in Primary Arthroscopy

Shoulder arthroscopy (29827) billed with separate debridement code (29822), Medicare considers debridement inclusive in the rotator cuff repair when performed in the same session. Billed as two claims; payer pays one, recoupment audit risk created for the other.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX applies current NCCI arthroscopy bundling edits before every claim. Separately billable procedures during arthroscopy are identified with Modifier 59 or XS where supported by clinical documentation. Inclusive procedures are never separately billed.

PATTERN 05

Post-Surgical Brace or DME Denied for Missing Medical Necessity

Knee brace (L1820) dispensed post-op. Claim submitted without detailed written order, ICD-10 linkage, or physician signature on the CMN. Medicare and commercial payers deny every DME claim that lacks complete documentation, often thousands of dollars per patient.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX manages orthopedic DME billing with correct HCPCS L-codes, complete detailed written orders, ICD-10 medical necessity linkage, and CMN documentation before every claim. Post-surgical brace and orthotic revenue is fully captured on every patient.

PATTERN 06

Bilateral Code Submitted Without Modifier 50

Bilateral knee injections performed. Single CPT submitted at 2 units without Modifier 50. Payer processes as two separate claims and denies the second as a duplicate. Or bilateral code submitted as two separate claims on same DOS, triggers duplicate claim denial and potential audit.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX applies Modifier 50 on bilateral procedures and submits as single line items where payer billing rules require, or as two separate claims with RT/LT modifiers where required. Payer-specific bilateral billing rules applied per claim, not generically.

THE EDUCATION

What Is Orthopedic Billing And Why U.S. Practices Are Leaving Revenue on the Table

Orthopedic billing is the most modifier-dependent, global-period-driven billing category in U.S. surgical medicine. Every error is expensive and most are invisible until they compound.

Orthopedic medical billing is a specialized back-office function that assigns diagnostic and procedure codes, submits and tracks insurance claims, manages denials and appeals, and posts patient payments specifically orthopedic practices ensuring reimbursement aligns with U.S. musculoskeletal treatment rules and American payer guidelines. What makes orthopedic billing uniquely complex in the U.S. healthcare system is the global surgery period the window after a surgical procedure during which follow-up services are bundled into the original procedure payment by Medicare and most major commercial payers. Most major orthopedic procedures carry a 90-day global period (joint replacements, rotator cuff repairs, spinal fusions). Minor procedures carry a 10-day period. Some carry none.

The consequence of getting this wrong: billing for post-surgical E/M visits during an active global period results in automatic denial. Not billing when you should because no one tracked when the window closed means permanent revenue loss. PMEX connects to your existing EHR, pulls procedure dates from your operative notes, and tracks every active global period across your entire patient panel automatically. The second major complexity: surgical modifier logic. Modifier 58 (staged procedure), modifier 78 (return to OR, related), modifier 79 (unrelated procedure during global), and modifier 57 (E/M on day of surgery) are the most frequently miscoded in orthopedic billing each with different documentation requirements and U.S. payer-specific consequences.

GLOBAL SURGERY PERIOD · THE RISK IN U.S ORTHOPEDICS

U.S Orthopedic Practices Lose $150K–$300K per Year to Global Period Errors They Never See Coming.

The global surgery period is how Medicare and most U.S. payers bundle post-surgical care into the original procedure payment. Billing a separate E/M visit or related service during an active global period without the correct modifier results in automatic denial. The claim looks like a duplicate to the payer's system.

The reverse costs just as much: not billing services that fall legitimately outside the global period because no one tracked when the window closed means that revenue is permanently lost. Most U.S. orthopedic billing teams manage this on spreadsheets or not at all.

PMEX connects to your existing EHR, pulls procedure dates from your signed operative notes, and tracks every active global period across your entire patient panel in real time auto-applying the correct modifier (58, 78, 79, 24) on every post-surgical claim before it's submitted.

90-Day Global

Major Surgical Procedures

Total knee (27447), total hip (27130), rotator cuff (29827), spinal fusion, femur ORIF. Post-surgical E/M visits during this window require Mod 24 or 79 or they're automatically denied by Medicare and major commercial payers.

10-Day Global

Minor Surgical Procedures

Arthrocentesis (20610), trigger point injections, minor repairs. A 10-day post-operative billing window applies shorter but still requires modifier awareness for related services billed by any provider.

0-Day Global

Endoscopies & Scope Procedures

Diagnostic arthroscopies and certain joint procedures carry no global period. Separately billable E/M services on the same day still require Mod 25 a modifier U.S. payers scrutinize aggressively.

PMEX tracks global periods across every active patient in your practice pulling procedure dates from your existing EHR. No separate data entry. No spreadsheets. No missed windows.

Common Questions

Orthopedic Billing Answered

Everything you need to know about PMEX orthopedic billing services

No. PMEX integrates directly with your existing EHR, Epic, Cerner, Athena, eClinicalWorks, NextGen, Modernizing Medicine, and 35+ others. Your clinical team keeps using the same system they know. PMEX connects to it, captures charges automatically, and manages all billing downstream. No migration, no retraining, no disruption. Most integrations are live within 3–5 business days.

PMEX manages the full MIPS workflow directly from your existing EHR data, selecting the highest-value quality measures for cardiology (CAD, heart failure, hypertension), tracking performance throughout the year, ensuring documentation meets CMS reporting requirements, and submitting data. Scoring below 75 triggers Medicare cuts; PMEX keeps you above threshold and captures available bonus payments averaging $90K+.

PMEX applies NCCI edits and cardiology-specific bundling logic before every claim submission. When a cardiologist performs multiple procedures in the same session, our coders determine which can be separately billed with modifiers (51, 59, XS) and which are considered inclusive, preventing both undercoding and triggering payer audits. NCCI rules are updated continuously in our scrubbing engine.

Yes. PMEX audits denied cardiology claims, identifies root causes (prior auth issues, modifier errors, bundling violations), and resubmits corrected claims within 48 hours. We also track denial patterns systematically, if the same modifier error is causing repeated denials, we fix it at the source so it stops happening across all future claims.

Yes. PMEX bills remote physiological monitoring for cardiac patients using CPT codes 99453, 99454, 99457, and 99458 plus device-specific codes. We manage the 16-day minimum monitoring threshold tracking and monthly claim generation, capturing recurring revenue from your existing cardiac monitoring program. Most practices we onboard have never billed these codes correctly.

PMEX Prior Auth manages pre-authorization for high-value cardiology procedures, catheterizations, pacemaker implants, EP studies, nuclear imaging, using clinical documentation pulled directly from your existing EHR. We submit with documentation attached, track status in real time, and alert scheduling when authorization is secured. Average approval: 36 hours. Zero scheduling cancellations due to auth gaps.

Yes. PMEX manages split billing for global, professional (modifier 26), and technical (modifier TC) components of diagnostic cardiology procedures, echocardiograms, stress tests, Holter interpretation, based on your practice's specific facility relationship. This is a frequently missed revenue element in cardiology practices that perform both components.

PMEX integrates with Epic, Cerner/Oracle Health, Athenahealth, eClinicalWorks, NextGen, Modernizing Medicine, Allscripts, Kareo, DrChrono, and 35+ additional EHR platforms. For cardiology-specific systems (Epic Cupid, Cerner CardioAdmin), we support the full charge capture and documentation workflow. Integration setup is typically complete within 3–5 business days.

Yes. All PMEX cardiology billing specialists hold AAPC certification with dedicated cardiology specialty training, not general medical billing. They know cath labs, echo reports, NCCI cardiology-specific bundles, and payer-specific cardiac procedure policies inside out. Cardiology coding is their specific expertise, not a rotation.

PMEX monitors every payment against your payer-specific contract rates and fee schedules. When a payment falls below your contracted rate, we identify the discrepancy, document the contract language, and file a formal appeal with the payer. Systematic underpayments, where a payer is consistently paying below contract for specific cardiology procedures, are escalated for contract renegotiation support.

Yes. PMEX codes telehealth cardiology consultations with correct POS codes (02 or 10), applicable modifiers, and documentation requirements per payer, staying current on CMS and commercial payer telehealth policies, which continue to evolve. We also handle remote patient monitoring billing for cardiac patients receiving virtual cardiac monitoring services.
